entries.before: Fly, Dock and Resume require live native sensing. Weak or lost contact suspends guidance and clears Auto Nav thrust; it does not brake blindly or resume automatically when the signal returns. Destination and progress are retained. Radar and LiDAR are never enabled automatically. Range and speed are unknown without a usable track. Sensor Operations skill uses the currently selected crew member aboard this ship, including with the panel closed.
entries.after: Fly, Dock and Resume require a live track from this ship's own sensors. Every switched-on sensor counts: optical, infrared, EM, radar and LiDAR signals combine as on the native map. If the target or a hazard near the route is too faint, Auto Nav switches on the fewest fitted sensors that fix it: non-emitting ones first, radar or LiDAR only when those are not enough. It tells you in the crew log and on the nav map, and switches them off when it finishes unless you changed them. Switch one off yourself and Auto Nav leaves it off until it finishes. Mod settings, Sensors > AutoEngage: All, Passive (never radar or LiDAR) or Off. Weak or lost target contact that no sensor can fix suspends guidance and clears Auto Nav thrust; it does not brake blindly or resume automatically when the signal returns. Destination and progress are retained, and sensors stay on while a flight is suspended. Weak contacts near the route are still avoided, with extra clearance. Asteroids can be flown to when sensed within 1,000 km. Range and speed are unknown without a usable track. Sensor Operations skill uses the currently selected crew member aboard this ship, including with the panel closed.

entries.before:
Navigation: Approach stops at the selected separation; Dock starts checked terminal RCS guidance. Approach & Dock binds the target and assigned ports, approaches 1 km beyond the protective hull-clearance radius, matches motion and rechecks before terminal handoff. Inside staging it uses terminal admission directly. Keep the native docking interface available for attachment; the hub never bypasses clearance, fees, consequences or port fit.

Closing speed is positive toward the target and negative when separating. Relative speed includes sideways drift. A dash means unavailable, including pending power or contact updates. Alignment is the existing terminal controller's ship-to-target heading error, not a measurement of port geometry.

Pursuit requires N2; the Fire page requires N3. N3 works independently during manual flight or coasting. Select the offensive target separately, choose its native weapon group and volley limit, then lift the cover and Engage. Auto Aim is separate. Cease Fire stops aiming and retains offensive hold while Follow continues. Return to Native explicitly releases that hold and may resume native autofire. Native power, arcs, aim, ammunition, reload, missile lock and weapon-mode restrictions still apply. Braking takes priority. If native guarded artwork is unavailable, Engage stays inhibited.

Systems controls take manual authority and clear automation before changing reactor flow/thrust. Native reactor readiness, limiter and no-wake restrictions still apply; this hub cannot start a cold reactor. Connected power is the native console's connected stored energy, not whole-ship generation. Use the native reactor and specialist instruments for startup, faults and detailed engineering.

Disengage clears commanded thrust and allows coasting; it is not an emergency brake. Combined docking and pursuit always suspend on loading. Resume rechecks the same module, target and ports. Page changes and display refresh never authorize commands.

If native flight intent blocks engagement, Disengage explicitly releases standard native autopilot, station-keeping and held thrust, clears saved switches on this ship's consoles and sets torch cycle to zero. Reactor power stays on; velocity and spin remain. Unknown AI and independent flight plugins must release themselves. Resume needs a suspended flight; Cease Fire needs active flight or fire control. N1 alone does not enable N2 pursuit or N3 weapons.
entries.after:
Navigation: Approach stops at your chosen separation. Dock uses RCS for the final approach. Approach & Dock keeps the selected target and ports, approaches a point 1 km beyond hull clearance, matches motion, then checks the docking approach. If already inside that point, it checks docking directly. Keep the navigation console open for final clamps. Clearance, fees and port fit still apply.

Closing speed is positive when moving towards the target, negative when moving away. Relative speed includes sideways drift. A dash means no current reading. Alignment is the difference between ship headings, not a measurement of the ports themselves.

N2 enables Rendezvous and Follow. N3 enables Fire, including during manual flight or coasting. Select a separate fire target, weapon group and volley limit; lift the cover and Engage. Auto Aim is a separate choice. Cease Fire stops aiming and holds offensive fire while Follow can continue. Return to Native releases the hold and may allow normal automatic firing again. Weapons still need power, ammunition, aim, range, clear firing arcs and any required missile lock. Braking takes priority. If the guarded switch cannot be displayed, Engage is blocked.

Systems controls disengage automation before changing reactor flow or thrust. The reactor must be ready; the thrust limiter and no-wake restrictions still apply. The hub cannot start a cold reactor. Stored energy means energy connected to this console, not total ship generation. Use reactor and specialist panels for startup and fault finding.

Disengage cuts commanded thrust; the ship keeps moving and spinning. Combined docking and pursuit pause after loading. Resume checks the original module, target and ports. Changing pages never issues a command.

If standard autopilot, station-keeping or held thrust blocks engagement, Disengage clears those controls on this ship and sets torch cycle to zero. Reactor power stays on. Other AI or flight mods must release control themselves. Resume needs a saved paused flight; Cease Fire needs active flight or fire control. N1 alone does not enable pursuit or weapons.

entries.before:
Rendezvous and Follow require N2.

Rendezvous matches motion and finishes. Follow maintains separation.

Weapons and optional aiming require N3 on the Fire page.
entries.after:
Rendezvous matches motion and finishes. Follow maintains separation. Both require N2.

Combat requires N2 + N3. Select a fire target and Use for aim on the Fire tab first. Enter Combat uses the speed and separation above, suspends the previous flight, and starts range matching and aiming. Engage weapons separately.

Braking, traffic avoidance and torch manoeuvres take priority over weapon facing. Cease Fire stops aiming and firing while range matching continues. Leave Combat to change movement settings; Resume the previous flight explicitly.

entries.reason: 0.22.0: reviewed coordinated navigation and Combat commands against implemented permission, exit and reload behaviour.
entries.before:
N3 Fire Control System: select a qualified offensive target and one native weapon group. Volleys (1–9) counts successful native batches, not projectiles or ammunition units; each batch contains the weapons ready at that instant. Engage requires the guarded switch. Weapons can operate during manual flight with Auto Aim off.

Auto Aim is a separate permission for RCS rotation while coasting, or a heading request during N2 Follow. Choose a weapon with Weapon > and Use for aim. Pilot thrust/yaw cancels aiming and firing. Braking and clearance take priority.

Cease Fire and volley completion retain offensive hold and stop Auto Aim; Follow continues. Return to Native explicitly releases the group and may allow native autofire. Defensive PDCs and deliberate manual fire remain native. Release the old group before changing groups.

Reload retains offensive hold only: targets, firing permission, remaining volleys and live aiming are never restored. Missing/stale readings are unavailable. Missiles require native automatic eligibility and a full native lock; decoys are excluded. No promised hit probability, intact boarding or crew survival. Native map, sensors and specialist weapon settings remain separate.
entries.after:
Select a tracked fire target and one weapon group. Volleys (1–9) counts successful firing batches: each batch fires the weapons ready at that moment, not one projectile per weapon. Lift the cover to Engage. With Auto Aim off, weapons can operate while you fly manually.

Auto Aim permits RCS turning while coasting, or requests a heading during Approach, Rendezvous, Follow or Combat. Choose a weapon with Weapon > and Use for aim. When aiming is active, pilot thrust or turning cancels aiming and firing. Braking and clearance take priority.

Cease Fire or the end of a volley order stops Auto Aim and keeps offensive fire on hold. Follow and Combat range matching can continue. Return to Native exits Combat and releases the hold and may allow normal automatic firing again. Defensive PDCs and deliberate manual fire still work normally. Choose an installed group from the picker. If FCS holds the old group, confirm its return to native control; the new group stays on hold. Left-click Volleys to increase; right-click to decrease. Both wrap between 1 and 9. Switched-off and damaged weapons remain listed but cannot fire.

Loading a save keeps fire on hold. It does not restore targets, firing permission, remaining volleys or aiming. Missing or stale readings mean unavailable. Missiles need permission for automatic fire and a full lock; decoys are excluded. Hits, intact boarding and crew survival are never guaranteed. Use the map, sensors and specialist weapon settings as usual.

hardcodedReview.scope: All src/Phobos*/**/*.cs (excluding build output); quoted prose, Text.Get callers, definition fields and panel text assignments inspected.
hardcodedReview.result: Player prose uses catalogues. Exception messages and logger strings retain diagnostic precision. Runtime names use equipment-names.json; enum-derived statuses and descriptions use dynamic catalogue families. Native widgets keep game-owned labels.
hardcodedReview.limitation: Lexical references are review aids, not a C# control-flow proof. Compatibility fallbacks without a direct lexical caller are identified separately.
